key_insight: Projected-space ADAPT-VQE generators do not always transfer faithfully to full-space implementations; exact equivalence requires target-space invariance ($QAP=0$).
engineering_relevance: Quantum circuit builders and VQE practitioners must audit representation equivalence separately from energy optimization because a circuit with the “same” amplitudes can produce a very different state and energy.
method: Defines a representation-equivalence audit for open-shell ADAPT-VQE using the condition $QAP=0$.
Compares projected-doublet ADAPT, same-angle full-space transfer, and full-space reoptimization on a CAS(15e,9o) Cu(II) benchmark.
Validates the framework with an independent NO benchmark and a spin-preserving generalized full-space construction.
evidence_signal: In the Cu(II) case, 274 of 323 candidate excitations violate equivalence; the projected result reaches 1.5719 m$E_h$, while same-angle transfer gives 464.730 m$E_h$ error and 0.07343 fidelity, and reoptimization reduces the best error only to 8.482 m$E_h$.
watch_item: The study is a validation framework rather than a new spin-adapted ADAPT algorithm, and circuit-synthesis checks still need separate verification from final-energy checks.
paper_title: From Projected Subspaces to Full-Space Implementations: Representation-Equivalence Audits for Open-Shell ADAPT-VQE
